name: shiftmap-min-max-reduce-an-eight-by-eight-blur-map
rationale:
Covers air.atomic.local.min.s.i32 and air.atomic.local.max.s.i32, the two threadgroup atomics with the most case-less corpus sources, together with the pixel-coordinate air.gather_texture_2d.v4f16 that feeds them. The kernel's static addrspace(3) [2 x atomic i32] is seeded to INT_MAX/INT_MIN by thread (0,0), reduced into by every thread, and read back after the second barrier, so a lost or mis-ordered atomic changes the answer.

Loop bound: both loops step the thread's texel origin by a whole grid, x by (gid.x+32)*4 and y by (gid.y+16)*4, and exit once that origin leaves the texture. On an 8x8 input the next origin is 128 and 64 texels out, so every thread runs exactly one iteration of each loop and the kernel is straight-line in practice.

Grid (2,2,1) in one threadgroup of (2,2,1) puts all four threads on the same two atomic slots and tiles the 8x8 input with four disjoint 4x4 blocks. Each thread gathers at its origin plus (1,1), (1,3), (3,1) and (3,3); the embedded sampler is coord::pixel with filter::nearest and clamp_to_edge, so the four bilinear footprints are the texel pairs {0,1} and {2,3} on each axis and together they are exactly the thread's 4x4 block. The extremes sit at the two far corners, 0.25 at texel (0,0) and 0.75 at texel (7,7): a footprint that is shifted, clamped or short of four gathers loses one of them and moves the result.

Exactness: every input texel is a multiple of 2^-5 in [0.25, 0.75], so multiplying by 65536 is an integer and the fast_floor and fast_ceil that follow are no-ops whatever variant runs them; the products stay under 49152, far inside i32. The reduction therefore yields min 16384 and max 49152, scaled back by 2^-16 to exactly 0.25 and 0.75. Their difference is 0.5, so the final fdiv is 1/0.5 = 2 and is exact under fast:: and precise:: alike. Expected texel (0,0) of the rgba32_float output is (0.25, 0.75, 0.5, 2.0).

name: nearest-pixel-sampler-at-texel-centres
rationale: A 4x2 grid samples a 4x2 rgba32_float texture through the constexpr sampler (coord::pixel, filter::nearest, address::clamp_to_edge) at float2(x, y) + 0.5, the centre of texel (x, y): an exact texel fetch (sampler.pixel_fetch, DESIGN D213). Texel (x, y) is (x + 4y, 2x, 3y, 0.5), so out[y * 4 + x] is that texel. The AIR has no loop.

name: precise-division-at-the-flush-boundary-and-midpoints
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): Metal's precise float division (no flag, compiled without fast math) at the edges a correctly rounded quotient must get right. Each of 512 threads writes x / y (words 1-3 keep the 0xAB poison). Lanes: 64 quotients exactly 2^-126 - 2^-150 (x = (2 - 2^-23) * 2^a over y = 2^(a + 127), either sign), a tie on the denormal grid that rounds to 2^-126, where rounding to 24 bits first keeps a denormal that a flush makes zero, and 32 quotients just below and 32 just above that value; 64 near the overflow threshold (2 - 2^-24) * 2^127; 160 within 2^-10 of an ulp (relative 2^-34) of a rounding midpoint; 64 divisors at or past 2^126; 32 denormal numerators or divisors; the rest random bit patterns without NaN exponents. The AIR has no loop.

name: write-through-a-storage-texture-selected-per-thread
rationale: Eight threads write (g, 1, 2, 3) at texel (g >> 1, 0) of storage texture a when g is odd and of b when g is even (texture.write.switch, DESIGN D18, D213). Both are 4x1 rgba32_float textures initially 0xab. The observation is the whole of a: texel k is (2k + 1, 1, 2, 3), so a write landing in the wrong texture or texel is visible. The AIR has no loop.

name: add-signed-bytes-into-unsigned-bytes-and-clamp
rationale: Metal ground truth for the four uncovered AIR symbols this kernel is made of: air.convert.s.v3i32.s.v3i8, air.convert.s.v3i32.u.v3i8, air.clamp.s.v3i32 and air.convert.u.v3i8.s.v3i32 (5 case-less sources). The kernel sign-extends a packed_char3 from buffer 0, zero-extends the packed_uchar3 already in buffer 1, adds them, clamps to [0, 255] and truncates back to three bytes, so every step is integer and the result is exact regardless of fast-math reassociation. Four texels pin both extensions and both clamp ends: texel 0 is char3(-100, -128, 127) over uchar3(200, 0, 255), whose x is 100 only if the signed source really sign-extends (zero-extending 0x9C gives 356, which clamps to 255) and the unsigned destination really zero-extends (sign-extending 0xC8 gives -56, so the sum would clamp to 0); its y saturates at the low end and its z at the high end. Texel 1 lands exactly on 255 without clamping and pins a -1 that would read 255 unsigned, texel 2 clamps only its y, and texel 3 stays inside the range untouched. The uint2 in buffer 2 is the (4, 1) grid extent the kernel bounds-checks against, so all four threads store.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-2x2-output

name: four-multisample-reads-at-two-samples
rationale: Metal ground truth for six uncovered multisample read families: air.read_texture_2d_ms.u.v4i16 (3 case-less corpus sources), air.read_texture_2d_ms.u.v4i32 (2), air.read_texture_2d_ms.s.v4i32 (2), air.read_texture_2d_ms.i16.v4f16 (2), air.read_texture_2d_ms.i16.u.v4i16 (2) and air.read_depth_2d_ms.f32 (2) -- 13 sources. A multisample read takes one operand an ordinary read does not, the sample index, and it is the operand a lowering can silently drop because every sample of a texel is a plausible answer for that texel. The four threads therefore read four different texels at two different samples, and every stored value encodes its own (x, y, sample) triple, so a read that ignored the sample index or took it from the coordinate lands a value the derivation places somewhere else. The two u.v4i16 symbols differ only in operand width -- .i16. is a ushort2 coordinate and ushort sample, the other uint2 and uint -- and they read the same texture through different channels, so a lowering that widened one wrongly disagrees with the other where both must be right. Every value is an integer well inside its type or an exact binary fraction.

name: constant-half4-zero
rationale: The fragment structurally ignores its position and three generated varyings and returns literal half4 zero, so one full-coverage invocation must replace every poisoned RGBA16Float lane with zero.

name: cube-texel-read-beside-a-cube-sample
rationale: A cube texel read on a cube the same kernel also direction-samples. SPIR-V has no cube texel fetch -- OpImageFetch forbids Dim Cube -- so read() is lowered as a sample along a direction aimed at the exact centre of the named texel, through a sampler the translator invents because no Metal argument supplies one. That descriptor is reported as SynthesizedReadSampler, and the executor had no arm for the kind at all: no consumer could build a pipeline for a module containing one, so this family had no case and could not have had one. The state the sampler must be bound with -- nearest at magnification, minification and between mip levels -- was recorded only in a comment in the lowering. The cube stays Dim Cube because it is sampled as well as read; a cube only read is declared as something SPIR-V can fetch and no sampler is invented. Faces 0-3 carry a distinct value per texel, so the four reads on them measure the face index, the in-face coordinate, and the direction the translator builds to reach that texel: 1, 12, 23, 34. Faces 4 and 5 are uniform, 41 and 54, and are what the two samples aim at along the exact +Z and -Z axes -- a sample at the centre of a uniform face is the same value under any filter or address mode, so those lanes measure the sampling path and nothing about cube corner conventions. Every value is a small integer, exact in binary32.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirteen-simd-primary

name: sample-an-argument-buffer-texture-through-constexpr-samplers
rationale: A 4x2 grid samples the 4x2 rgba32_float source texture of constant argument buffer 0 {texture2d<float> source; texture2d<float, access::write> target;} through two constexpr samplers (sampler.heap.sample and sampler.heap.pixel_fetch, DESIGN D162, D213): a normalized nearest clamp-to-edge sample at ((x + 0.5) / 4, (y + 0.5) / 2) and a nearest pixel sample at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5), both the centre of texel (x, y), and writes the first plus twice the second at texel (x, y) of target (field 8, initially 0xab): 3 source(x, y). Texel (x, y) of source is (x + 4y, 0.25x, 0.5y, 1), so target(x, y) = (3 (x + 4y), 0.75x, 1.5y, 3). The AIR has no loop.

name: a-kernel-s-barrier-orders-an-object-buffer-read-after-a-mesh-buffer-write
rationale: icb_enc_stages sets command 0's pipeline to mesh_barrier_writer's (without rasterization), its mesh buffer 0 to its buffer 1, and a mesh draw of one threadgroup; and command 1's barrier, its pipeline to icb_object_reader's under icb_mesh_triangle, its object buffer 0 to its buffer 1, and a mesh draw of one thread. The writer stores (3, 2, 1, 7) into word 0; behind the barrier the reader reads it and writes it doubled plus one, (7, 5, 3, 15), into word 1.

name: a-kernel-s-mesh-draw-of-threadgroups-runs-under-its-inherited-pipeline-and-buffers
rationale: icb_enc_groups encodes command 0's mesh draw of 3 by 2 threadgroups of 4 threads into a buffer of mesh draws of threadgroups that inherits its pipeline and buffers; executed under icb_mesh_marks with the case's buffer 1 at mesh buffer 0, each of the 6 threadgroups marks its word with its position, the grid's threadgroups and its threads; the seventh word stays as the bytes 0xab.

name: a-kernel-s-mesh-draw-of-threads-runs-with-its-own-mesh-buffer
rationale: icb_enc_threads sets command 0's mesh buffer 0 to its buffer 1 and a mesh draw of 12 by 4 threads in threadgroups of 4 by 2, on a buffer of mesh draws of threads that inherits only its pipeline; executed under icb_mesh_marks, each of the 3 by 2 threadgroups marks its word with its position, the grid's threadgroups and its threads; the seventh word stays as the bytes 0xab.

name: a-kernel-s-reset-leaves-the-second-mesh-draw-running-nothing
rationale: icb_enc_reset encodes command 0's mesh draw of 3 by 2 threadgroups of 4 threads and command 1's of 12 by 4 threads in threadgroups of 4 by 2, then resets command 1, on a buffer of both mesh draw kinds that inherits its pipeline and buffers; executed under icb_mesh_marks, only command 0's threadgroups mark their words (threads 4 by 1), and the seventh word stays as the bytes 0xab.

name: linked-single-lane-mx-dequantize
no_effect: The linked destination callback is a no-op by design, so the destination element keeps its authored bytes while the dequantization path runs.
rationale: One invocation reads exactly four packed quantized bytes and one shared scale byte from the two authored device-array inputs. The exact linked primary float4 destination is the retained no-op callback; the sole poisoned destination element therefore remains byte-exact and proves the linked callback contract while the dequantization path executes.

name: sixteen-lanes-dequantize-through-the-public-linked-destination
rationale: Reaching variant of the single-lane case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose linked destination callback was the retained postfixPrimary_4xf, which writes nothing. This case links the public module validation/fixtures/public/linked/mps_postfix_primary_4xf_to_last_buffer (owned MSL, DESIGN D431 item 2): it stores the float4 at elements coordinate.x to coordinate.x + 3 of the kernel's buffer table's last array (constant 122 = 3 gives the kernel three arrays, and the callback the count 3), so each dequantized value reaches the destination. Sixteen threads (one threadgroup) each read 3 packed bytes of FP6 E3M2 codes at 3 * gid.x from array 0 and one scale byte at (4 gid.x) >> 5 from array 1 (E8M0 scale bytes 0x76 (0.00195312), 0x81 (4), one per 32 elements); thread gid.x writes elements 4 gid.x to 4 gid.x + 3 of array 2 (256 bytes, poisoned 0xab before), so every thread's four words are observed and none overlaps another's. The codes spread over the format's nonzero finite encodings (no zero of either sign, whose sign the kernels' fast math leaves unspecified, and no NaN or infinity); every decoded value times its scale is a normal float, exact, 64 distinct words. Straight-line code: no loop.

name: compact-live-depth-bins-by-a-two-level-lane-prefix-sum
rationale: A 32x32 threadgroup is 32 SIMD groups of 32 lanes, and thread_index_in_threadgroup is y*32 + x, so SIMD group s is exactly image row s. Each lane flags its texel with air.convert.u.i1.f.f16 (zero) or the shader's own NaN bit test, air.simd_sum.u.i16 counts the flags per row, one air.simd_prefix_inclusive_sum.u.i16 turns those 32 row counts into row bases, and a second one gives each lane its rank inside its row. The compaction then writes every live texel index at its rank, which is what makes both prefix sums observable: a wrong base or a wrong within-row rank moves entries rather than changing their values. 329 of the 1024 texels are flagged -- some +0.0, some -0.0 and some quiet NaN, so a > 0 test or a bit-equality test against positive zero would both disagree -- and the surviving 695 indices land in ascending order over the first 1390 bytes, with the tail of the buffer left at its poisoned initial value. Every value is an exact ushort, so nothing here has rounding or association freedom.

name: depthwise-conv-grad-data-k4x4-s2x2-odd-width-writes-every-column
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-work case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero sizes fail every thread's bounds check. User constant 124 = 3 << 28: channel axis 3 (coordinate (x, y, d, c)), no odd offsets, no gradient accumulation (the write goes to postfixPrimary_f); constant 112 = 0 (padding mode 0). The data gradient's size (fwdParams.srcSize) is (W, H, D, C) = (5, 4, 1, 2), the gradient's (3, 2, 1, 2), zero offsets. One threadgroup of 3x2x2 threads: each computes the 2x2 output block at (2 gid.x, 2 gid.y) of channel gid.z through the unrolled 4x4 stride-2 kernel. Threads with x0 = 0 or 2 take the full-block path and write all four pixels; threads with x0 = 4 (x0 + 1 = 5 is outside W) take the edge path, which writes only the two pixels of column 4. The coordinate's first component is x, so words 0 to 4 are written and words 5 to 7 keep the 0xab fill. The retained modules of the source callbacks the case links return constants (prefixSecondary_f and prefixTertiary_f 0.0; the only retained modules of those functions), so every product is 0.0 and every sum exactly +0.0 in any order; every writer of a word stores that same value, so the observed words do not depend on write order. The variant observes the loops, the bounds checks and the written coordinates through the linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec, table entry 1 at the coordinate's first component), not data-dependent arithmetic. The kernel has no loop over data (the 4x4 taps are unrolled).

name: linked-zero-work-depthwise-conv-grad-data-k4x4-s2x2

rationale: Zero dimensions bound the one-thread depthwise gradient-data invocation while exact callback modules provide all direct linkage. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fifteen-simd-primary

name: one-output-pixel-four-channel-fma-accumulation
rationale:
First coverage of air.fma.f16, whose 108 case-less corpus sources are the largest uncovered count reachable by an exact byte comparison. The AIR is an Espresso v9 half-accumulating convolution; the function constants collapse it to its smallest live shape -- one 1x1 kernel tap, one convolution group, unit strides, no upsampling, no k-splitting -- so a single invocation at gid (0,0,0) computes one output pixel of four channels from four input channels. That is exactly sixteen chained air.fma.f16 calls, four per output channel, plus the bias add. F_activation is 3, which is the switch's default arm and applies no activation, so the module's five air.tanh.f16 calls stay out of the executed region: half tanh is one of the intrinsics whose fast:: and precise:: Metal variants disagree, and an exact comparison could not survive it.

Every authored value is a small integer, which is what makes the comparison exact rather than approximate. src is [1,2,3,4]; the four weight rows are [1,2,3,4], [5,6,7,8], [-1,3,-5,7] and [10,20,30,40], giving channel sums 30, 70, 18 and 300; the biases are [1000,-1000,7,0.5], so the answer is [1030,-930,25,300.5]. Every individual product and every running partial sum -- 1, 5, 14, 30 / 5, 17, 38, 70 / -1, 5, -10, 18 / 10, 50, 140, 300 -- is an exactly representable binary16 value, and so is each final sum (binary16 holds every integer to 2048, and 300.5 sits on a quarter-ulp grid). The result therefore does not depend on the order the four products are accumulated or on whether fast math reassociates the dependent fma chain, so a mismatch here is a lowering difference and not a rounding one.

The output buffer starts as eight poison bytes, so a kernel that returned through any of the four early exits at %34, %41, %46 or %378 without storing would be visible rather than silently passing. The distinct weight rows make each of the four accumulators independent: reading one output channel's weights for another would return 30 where -930 is written.

execution_safety is authored_bounded. All three loops are bounded by authored values: the kernel loops run F_kernel_size_y = 1 and F_kernel_size_x = 1 times, and the channel-block loop compares against end_k_split - start_k_split, which the params set to one block.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bins
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. The fixed channel loop advances its literal selector through the entry’s finite component count before exiting; it has no input-dependent trip count. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element, while the exact callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. One-bin histogram parameters force each active channel to bin zero and make the poisoned counters observable byte-exactly.

name: nan-model-half-operations-and-widening-of-nan-operands-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_half_fast (nan_half's program under the default fast math, the flagged state of the half classes; DESIGN D293): lane i reads the half patterns a, b, t, c and writes 32 words: float(a) and float(b) (fpext); then two half results per word: a - b, a / b, a * b + c (llvm.fmuladd), sin to ldexp as nan_functions computes them on half, fmin, fmax, fabs, min3, max3, median3, clamp(a, b, t), sign, saturate, copysign(a, b), fmod(a, b), -a, a * b, a + b; then float(t), float(c), and the patterns. Lanes: each half NaN (quiet and signaling of either sign, payloads 0, 1, 2, 0xaa, 0x155, 0x1fe, 0x1ff) as a and as b, four as t and as c, two NaNs, operands outside each operation's domain and the NaN-generating forms (0 * inf, inf - inf, 0 / 0, inf / inf, fmod of an infinity or by zero, mix of opposite infinities), the infinities, +-65504, zeros, denormals, and controls. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: flat-one-pixel-half-copy

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: constant-half4-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns a constant half4 to attachment zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned RGBA16Float pixel.

name: srgb-encode-of-every-half-and-a-2-14-float-grid
rationale: Metal's sRGB encode over a dense sweep. STATUS wave 11 owes 'pack rounding/sRGB'. D57.10 encodes a color channel with the MSL transfer (12.92 c below 0.0031308, else 1.055 c^(1/2.4) - 0.055) and rounds 255 * that to nearest even. D57.10 leaves open whether pack_float_to_srgb_unorm4x8 rounds half up instead, as the MSL texture rule spells it. D110.5 found that the decode goes through a 12-bit table, so the encode may too. Thread t = 0..5503 writes two words. Word 2t is pack_float_to_srgb_unorm4x8 of (3t, 3t + 1, 3t + 2, 3t) * 2^-14: every multiple of 2^-14 in [0, 1.0078], exact. The encode's narrowest byte step is about 1.24 * 2^-12 wide, so every step gets at least four samples. Word 2t + 1 is pack_half_to_srgb_unorm4x8 of the half patterns (3t, 3t + 1, 3t + 2, 3t): every half in [0, 1], and on to 2.25. That is the whole domain of the half encode below 1. The alpha channel is linear and reads 3t * 2^-14 (the half pattern 3t). D57.10 predicts RNE(255 * srgb(c)) for c in [0, 1] and 255 above 1. An encode through a table would put some byte boundaries off the transfer's, by up to half a table step. Compiled with the default fast math, as the corpus's packs are.
